links.outcome: Agreement between ChatGPT and consultant decisions on retrospective hip fracture cases
links.effect: Initial agreement low (κ = 0.03, 95% CI -0.11 to 0.19); validation cohort agreement κ = 0.29 (95% CI -0.04 to 0.60), not significantly different from initial.
links.quote: ChatGPT did not reliably replicate orthopaedic consultant decision-making for intracapsular NOF fractures.

links.outcome: Generalization of in-session-adjusted ChatGPT agreement to independent validation dataset
links.effect: After in-session adjustment κ = 0.93 (95% CI 0.84-1.00) in primary cohort; in validation cohort agreement fell to κ = 0.29 (95% CI -0.04 to 0.60, p = 0.06).
links.quote: Although in-session adjustments produced high superficial concordance, this effect did not generalize to an independent dataset.

unlisted_practices: Providing in-session consultant feedback to the LLM to adjust its recommendations (found to give superficial, non-generalizable concordance)

screen.reason: The study retrospectively evaluates the performance and agreement of ChatGPT compared to orthopaedic consultant decisions using de-identified clinical vignettes/records. It does not evaluate a deployed implementation safeguard or operational practice.
